summary: Okanogan NF summit site of an L-4 lookout cab built in 1931 and removed or destroyed in 1952; no source describes a standing lookout today.

facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1952 (sources differ on which); no source describes a standing lookout today

staffing.as_of: 1935 (last named lookout found in the sources read)

visit.trail_note: Willhite describes a 5.2-mile one-way route from the Twisp River road with about 4,400 feet of gain; no source says whether the site is open to visitors

events.note: L-4 cab built (Firetower.org, FireLookout.com, Willhite); Willhite notes a camp probably stood there before
Grover Brown named as the lookout in 1932 (Willhite)
Wenatchee World reports 11 large sending and receiving sets being installed at Okanogan and the Midnight Mountain station
Colin "Scotty" Gillies listed as known lookout personnel for 1933-1935 (FireLookout.com)
Panoramic photos taken from the roof (Willhite); Forest Lookouts gives May 26, 1936 for panorama photos
Firetower.org and Willhite say removed; FireLookout.com says destroyed
Registered November 18, 2012 as US 1454, WA 354; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org and Willhite say the cab was removed in 1952; FireLookout.com says destroyed that year. The sources agree on the year and disagree on how the cab ended. Not resolved; the story gives both.
Willhite dates the roof panoramas to 1934; Forest Lookouts dates panorama photos to May 26, 1936. Not resolved; both are reported.
A 1931 map caption and the Forest Lookouts header use Chelan National Forest; Firetower.org and FireLookout.com use Okanogan National Forest. The sources do not say when the name changed.

notes_for_editor: Four sources cover the same 1931-1952 span, but the story is thin on staffing (only 1932 and 1933-1935 names). The removed-or-destroyed question in 1952 is unresolved. The 'Pole still sticking up' caption is undated and may not describe the site now. Access level is omitted because no source says whether the site is public or closed. Elevation 7,481 ft (Firetower.org) and 7,480 ft (Willhite) are treated as the same figure and not used in the story. The brief's 'ground' kind is consistent with the 1950 survey note that the mark sat on the roof peak, so no correction is proposed.
